title: The Wizard of the Emerald City
author: Alexander Volkov
short_summary: A girl named Ellie and her little dog are swept away by a cyclone to a magical land, where a falling house accidentally defeats a wicked witch. To find a way home, Ellie sets off down a road of yellow bricks toward the Emerald City, where a mysterious wizard is said to grant wishes — joined by a scarecrow who wants a brain, a tin woodman who wants a heart, and a cowardly lion who wants courage.
extended_summary:
A girl named Ellie and her little dog are swept away by a cyclone to a magical land, where a falling house accidentally defeats a wicked witch. To find a way home, Ellie sets off down a road of yellow bricks toward the Emerald City, where a mysterious wizard is said to grant wishes — joined by a scarecrow who wants a brain, a tin woodman who wants a heart, and a cowardly lion who wants courage.

Along the way, the friends face a wicked witch who controls flying monkeys and tries to stop them from reaching the city. When they finally meet the Wizard, they discover his power is not what it seems — and that each of them already had what they were searching for all along, inside themselves.

questions.prompt: What does Ellie follow to reach the Emerald City?
questions.explanation: The road of yellow bricks leads all the way to the Emerald City.

questions.prompt: Match each character to what they want.
questions.explanation: Each companion is searching for exactly the quality they feel they lack.

questions.prompt: Each companion discovers that what they were searching for was inside them all ___.
questions.explanation: The story's twist is that the brain, heart, courage, and way home were never really missing.

questions.prompt: Which companion's wish do you relate to most, and why?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — each wish reflects something most people want at some point.

questions.prompt: What accidentally defeats the wicked witch at the very start of the story?

options: Ellie's house, carried by the cyclone, lands on her
The Tin Woodman chops through her spell
The Lion roars her out of the kingdom

questions.explanation: It's about the least heroic-looking defeat possible — a falling house — which is exactly why it takes everyone by surprise, witch included.

questions.prompt: Ellie follows the road of yellow bricks toward the ___ City, where a wizard is said to grant wishes.
questions.explanation: It's right there in the title — the whole journey is aimed at one glowing green city.

questions.prompt: Put the journey to the Emerald City in order.

items: A cyclone sweeps Ellie and her dog into a magical land
Ellie sets off down the road of yellow bricks, joined one by one by the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion
The friends face a second wicked witch and her flying monkeys
The group finally reaches the Wizard, and learns his power isn't what it seemed

questions.explanation: Each companion joins the road trip before the real danger — the flying monkeys — shows up to test them.

questions.prompt: Match each companion to what they discover by the end.

right: Was clever all along, brain or not
Had a caring heart the whole time
Was brave exactly when it counted
Had the way home inside her the whole time

questions.explanation: The twist for every single companion is the same shape: what they were searching for outside themselves was already inside them.

questions.prompt: Sort each companion by what they believe they're missing.

content.groupA: Believes they're missing something about their mind or heart
content.groupB: Believes they're missing courage or a way home

options.label: Tin Woodman, who wants a heart
Ellie, who wants to go home

questions.explanation: The four wishes split neatly into two kinds of 'missing piece' — but the story's answer to all four turns out to be the same.

questions.prompt: If you could ask the Wizard for one thing, like Ellie's companions did, what would it be — and do you think, like them, you might already have it?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the story's whole point is that the thing you think you're missing might already be closer than you'd guess.
